title: bareink dataset
description: Numbers described by what they mean. bareink picks the chart (or a table, or number cards) from this description; never pick a chart type yourself. Put the measures' values in rows, one object per period, category or item.

title.description: The takeaway as a sentence, e.g. 'Three categories take 71% of outflows'. Used as the accessible name of the chart.

key.description: Field in each row that holds the row's label, e.g. 'month'.

label.description: Human name of the dimension, e.g. 'Month'.

kind.description: time: ordered periods (months, weeks, years), oldest first. category: things to compare (expense categories, products, regions). stage: steps from a total to a result, such as revenue minus costs to profit, with deductions as negative numbers. record: a list of individual items such as invoices or transactions.

measures.description: The numbers in each row. More than 3, or measures in different units, become a table.

key.description: Field in each row that holds this number. Unique, and different from dimension.key.

unit.description: currency: money in whole units, not thousands. percent: 0 to 100, not 0 to 1. count: people, items, orders. number: anything else. text: a non-numeric column, which makes a table.

nature.description: flow: an amount that happens during each period and could be summed (revenue, inflows, outflows, sales). level: a stock read at a point in time that should not be summed (balance, price, headcount, occupancy, average ticket). signed: a result whose sign is the point (net result, profit or loss, variance).

openKey.description: Optional field with an amount still open or expected in the same period (unpaid invoices), drawn hatched on top of the paid amount.

rows.description: One object per period, category, stage or item, in display order (time: oldest first). Each row holds the dimension label and one value per measure; use null for a missing value, never 0.

partOfWhole.description: True when the rows are parts of one whole and the measure is a percent of it (adds up to 100 or less).

forecastFrom.description: Index of the first row that is a forecast and not an actual. Forecast rows are drawn hatched or dashed.

reference.description: A reference line, such as an average, a target or current capacity.

alertAbove.description: Color bars above the reference as an alert.

highlight.description: Row indexes whose value gets a direct label, usually the ones your answer mentions.

muted.description: Row indexes drawn in grey, for rows that are not really part of the comparison.

uncertain.description: Row indexes of parts of a whole whose classification is uncertain, drawn hatched.

totalRows.description: Stage rows that are totals rather than steps. Defaults to the first and last row.

keepOrder.description: Keep the categories in the given order instead of sorting by size.

markCumulative.description: Mark running totals on a part-of-a-whole bar.
